lessons.title: Il discorso indiretto libero: la voce senza virgolette
lessons.learn: Free indirect discourse lets a character's words into the narration with no quotation marks: the tense and the pronouns stay with the narrator, while the questions, the exclamations and the evaluations belong to the character. Italian novels run on it, and so does a report that wants to name a view without adopting it.

vocab.en: free indirect discourse
the narrating voice
exclamation

grammar.title: Free indirect frame
grammar.pattern: sarebbe arrivato tardi, lo sapeva · perché non aveva chiamato? · che sciocco era stato
grammar.explain: Sarebbe arrivato tardi, lo sapeva. Perché non aveva chiamato prima? Che sciocco era stato. No reporting verb, no colon: the modality (sarebbe, the exclamation) marks the voice as the character's, while the tenses stay inside the narration.

examples.t: Sarebbe arrivato tardi, lo sapeva.
examples.r: sah-REB-beh ahr-ree-VAH-toh TAR-dee, loh sah-PEH-vah.
examples.en: He would arrive late, he knew it.

examples.t: Perché non aveva chiamato prima?
examples.r: per-KEH nohn ah-VEH-vah kyah-MAH-toh PREE-mah?
examples.en: Why had he not called earlier?

examples.t: Che sciocco era stato.
examples.r: keh SHOHK-koh EH-rah STAH-toh.
examples.en: What a fool he had been.

mistakes.why: Free indirect discourse drops the reporting verb and the colon; the viewpoint carries them.

grammar.title: Normative frame

lessons.title: La mediazione: rendere accessibile senza tradire
lessons.learn: A mediator does two jobs at once: make the text usable — «in parole semplici: la misura entra in vigore a gennaio» — and record the loss. «Il testo dice dispositivo: qui vale misura» is a note, not a failure. Accessibility with no trace of the compromise is not mediation; it is rewriting.

grammar.title: Mediation frame
grammar.pattern: in parole semplici, … · il testo dice …, qui vale … · la nota del mediatore segnala …
grammar.explain: In parole semplici, la misura entra in vigore a gennaio. Il testo dice «dispositivo»: qui vale «misura». La nota del mediatore segnala ciò che si perde. The plain version and the record of the loss travel together.

examples.t: In parole semplici, la misura entra in vigore a gennaio.
examples.r: een pah-ROH-leh SEM-plee-chee, lah mee-ZOO-rah EN-trah een vee-GOH-reh ah jen-NAH-yoh.
examples.en: In plain words, the measure comes into force in January.

examples.t: Il testo dice «dispositivo»: qui vale «misura».
examples.r: eel TES-toh DEE-cheh dee-spoh-zee-TEE-voh: kwee VAH-leh mee-ZOO-rah.
examples.en: The text says 'dispositivo': here it means 'measure'.

examples.t: La nota segnala ciò che si perde.
examples.r: lah NOH-tah seh-NYAH-lah choh keh see PER-deh.
examples.en: The note flags what is lost.

culture.text: Bureaucratic Italian loves the noun: «la messa in atto della riforma» hides an actor, a verb and a responsibility. C1 work is learning to un-nominalise — to read «procedere all'aggiornamento» and hear «aggiornare» — and to write in a register that stays impersonal without disappearing entirely.

reading.text: La relazione indica che «la messa in atto del dispositivo sarà oggetto di valutazione». Tradotto in italiano corrente: qualcuno dovrà verificare se la misura funziona, e la relazione non dice chi. È esattamente questa vaghezza che la nota di sintesi attacca: per ogni frase passiva si scrivono il verbo, il soggetto e la data.
reading.gloss: The report states that 'the implementation of the scheme will be the subject of an evaluation'. Translated into ordinary Italian: somebody will have to check whether the measure works, and the report does not say who. It is exactly that vagueness that the summary note attacks: for every passive sentence, write the verb, the subject and the date.

task.title: Un-nominalise one administrative paragraph
task.instructions: Take a real Italian administrative sentence you have received — a letter, a notice, a form — and rewrite it three times: as it was written, in plain Italian with a subject and a verb, and as a three-line memo that names who does what by when. List every noun phrase you had to unpack; that list is your C1 vocabulary.
